blog.titolo: What does an SEO specialist do?

lezioni.titolo: What SEO is and how Google works

blocchi.testo: When you search on Google you see two kinds of results. Ads, marked «Sponsored», are paid for every click: that's the SEA job. Organic results are free: Google ranks them on its own, based on how well each page answers the search. SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is the work of getting a site's pages to appear high in the organic results. Today, for some searches, Google also shows an AI-written summary (AI Overviews) that cites some pages as sources.
blocchi.esempio: You search «organic green tea»: at the top, two ads from shops that pay, below them the organic results. Cinque Foglie wants to be among the organic ones without paying for every click.

domande.testo: Which of these is an organic result?

opzioni.t: A page that appears without the «Sponsored» label

domande.spiegazione: Ads are marked «Sponsored». The first position can be an ad too.

blog.titolo: What does an SEO specialist do?

blocchi.titolo: How Google finds and ranks pages
blocchi.testo: Google works in three phases. Crawling: a program (Googlebot) follows links and reads pages. Indexing: Google saves the pages it finds useful in its archive, the index. Ranking: when someone searches, Google picks the most useful pages from the index and puts them in order. A page that isn't crawled or doesn't make it into the index can't appear, however beautiful it is.
blocchi.esempio: A new Cinque Foglie product page with no links pointing to it risks not being found by Googlebot, and so never appearing.

voci: Indexing: the page goes into the archive
Ranking: the page appears in a search
domande.spiegazione: First Google has to read the page, then save it, and only then can it show it.

blog.titolo: How Google finds and ranks pages

blocchi.titolo: The three parts of the job
blocchi.testo: SEO has three parts. Content: choosing the right searches and writing pages that answer them well, with clear titles, descriptions and copy. Technical: making sure Google can read the site without obstacles, meaning fast pages, no errors, tidy URLs. Authority: other trusted websites talking about us and linking to our site (backlinks).
blocchi.esempio: A cooking blog post recommending Cinque Foglie's matcha with a link is authority; a product page that loads fast on phones is technical; a guide on how to brew Sencha is content.

domande.testo: Match each activity to the part of the job.
coppie: Writing a guide on how to brew Sencha
Getting a link from a cooking blog
domande.spiegazione: Content = what you write; technical = how Google reads the site; authority = what others say about you.

blog.titolo: What does an SEO specialist do?

blocchi.testo: SEO work is measured with four numbers, read in Google Search Console. Impressions: how many times a page appears in the results. Clicks: how many times someone clicks it. CTR: clicks divided by impressions, as a percentage. Average position: where it appears in the ranking. Then, with Google Analytics, you see what happens after the click: visits, orders, revenue.
blocchi.esempio: The green teas page has 10,000 impressions and 100 clicks: the CTR is 100 / 10,000 = 1%. Out of 100 people who see it, only one clicks.

domande.testo: A page has 2,000 impressions and 60 clicks. What's the CTR?
Impressions count how many people visited the page.
domande.spiegazione: Impressions count how many times the page appeared in the results, even if nobody clicked.

riepilogo: SEO gets a site into the organic results, without paying for every click.
Google crawls, indexes and then ranks pages.
The job has three parts (content, technical, authority) and is measured with impressions, clicks, CTR and position.

finali.testo: A page never appears on Google, not even when searching its exact title. What's your first suspicion?

opzioni.t: That it isn't in Google's index

finali.spiegazione: If a page doesn't appear at all, first check that Google has crawled and indexed it.

finali.testo: SEO and SEA are the same thing.
finali.spiegazione: SEO works on free organic results; SEA on paid ads.

finali.testo: Where do you read a site's impressions, clicks and CTR?
finali.spiegazione: Search Console shows what happens on Google; Analytics what happens after the click.

parole: The work of getting a site into Google's organic results.
The archive of pages Google can show.
Clicks divided by impressions: how many people click out of 100 who see the result.
A link from another website to ours.

blocchi.testo: A keyword is what a person types into Google. Volume is how many times a month it's searched. A high-volume keyword can bring the most visits, but usually has more competition; a longer, more specific keyword has less volume but more decided people. Each page gets one main keyword and a few close ones.
blocchi.esempio: «green tea» gets lots of searches but is generic; «organic sencha» gets fewer, but people searching it already know what they want.

domande.testo: Which keyword brings people more ready to buy?
domande.spiegazione: The more specific the search, the more the person knows what they want, even if the volume is lower.

blocchi.testo: Behind every search there's an intent, meaning what the person really wants. Informational: they want to understand («how to brew sencha»). Commercial: they compare before choosing («best green tea»). Transactional: they want to buy («organic sencha price»). Navigational: they're looking for a specific site («cinque foglie»). Google shows pages that match the intent: guides for an informational search, product pages for a transactional one.
blocchi.esempio: For «how to brew sencha» a product page never ranks: Google prefers a guide. For «organic sencha price» it's the other way round.

domande.testo: Match each search to its intent.
domande.spiegazione: Ask yourself what the person wants to do right after the search: learn, compare, buy or go to a specific site.

blocchi.testo: Each page should answer one specific intent. If two pages on the same site target the same search, they compete: Google alternates between them and neither ranks. It's called keyword cannibalisation. You fix it by giving each page a different job and linking them together.
blocchi.esempio: The guide «Sencha: what it is and how to brew it» explains; the product page «Organic Sencha green tea» sells. The guide links to the product page for people who want to buy.

domande.testo: Two pages targeting the same search help the site appear more often.
domande.spiegazione: They split the clicks and Google doesn't know which to choose: usually neither ranks.

blocchi.testo: The title is the blue title in Google's results: it should contain the keyword, say what people will find when they click and stay within about 580 pixels (60 characters). The meta description is the grey text below: 100-160 characters that persuade people to click. It doesn't improve rankings, but it increases clicks. The H1 is the big heading on the page, read by visitors.
blocchi.esempio: Title «Organic Sencha green tea, loose leaf | Cinque Foglie»; description «Organic Japanese Sencha, harvested in spring. How to brew it, and delivery in 24 hours.»; H1 «Organic Sencha».

domande.testo: Which title is better for the Sencha product page?

opzioni.t: Organic Sencha green tea, loose leaf | Cinque Foglie
Sencha sencha green tea sencha best sencha

domande.spiegazione: It says what you're buying, contains the keyword once and ends with the brand.

domande.testo: What is the meta description for?

opzioni.t: Persuading people who see the result to click

domande.spiegazione: Google doesn't use it for ranking, but a clear description increases clicks.

blog.titolo: Title tags and meta descriptions: how to write them

blocchi.testo: Google rewards content written for people: useful, clear, written by someone who knows the topic. Its guidelines use the acronym E-E-A-T: experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trustworthiness. For a food shop there are also legal rules: in the European Union you can't promise unauthorised health effects (Regulation EC 1924/2006), such as «burns fat» or «detox».
blocchi.esempio: «Our Sencha is brewed at 70-80 °C, for 1-2 minutes» is useful and true. «The Sencha that makes you lose weight» is banned and loses trust.

domande.testo: Which sentences can Cinque Foglie use on a product page?
domande.spiegazione: The first two describe the product. The others are unauthorised health claims: banned for a food.

riepilogo: Each page has one main keyword and answers one specific intent.
Two pages on the same search compete with each other: that's cannibalisation.
Title and description get clicks; content must be useful and follow the rules.

finali.spiegazione: The person wants to learn something, not buy straight away.

finali.testo: To rank on Google it's worth repeating the keyword many times in the title.
finali.spiegazione: Repeating it looks like spam: Google may rewrite the title and people click less.

finali.testo: The Sencha guide and product page compete for «sencha green tea». What do you do?

opzioni.t: Give each page a different intent and link them together
Copy the same text into both

finali.spiegazione: That way the guide answers people looking for information and the product page answers people buying.

parole: What the person searching really wants to do.
Two pages on the same site competing for the same search.
The grey text under the title in the results.

blocchi.titolo: Getting a page into (or out of) Google
blocchi.testo: The «noindex» meta robots tag asks Google not to show a page: it's used for the cart, account area and service pages. The robots.txt file, instead, tells Google which parts of the site not to crawl. Careful: if a page is blocked in robots.txt, Google can't read its noindex; to remove a page from the results you use noindex, not robots.txt.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie's cart has a noindex: that's fine. If the noindex ended up on a category by mistake, that category would disappear from Google.

domande.testo: Match each tool to what it does.
coppie: Asks not to show the page in the results
Asks not to crawl part of the site
domande.spiegazione: Noindex works on indexing, robots.txt on crawling.

domande.testo: An e-commerce cart should appear on Google.
domande.spiegazione: Nobody searches for it and it's no use to people arriving from Google: it gets a noindex.

blog.titolo: Noindex, robots.txt and canonical: the differences

blocchi.testo: When a page changes URL or is removed, you use a redirect. A 301 is permanent: Google passes the old page's value to the new one. A 302 is temporary. If a URL no longer exists and there's no redirect, anyone opening it gets a 404 error. A redirect should always point to the most similar page, and without chains (a redirect leading to another redirect).
blocchi.esempio: Classic Earl Grey has been replaced by the organic one: the old URL should be redirected with a 301 to the new product page, not to the home page.

domande.testo: A product has been removed for good and there's one that replaces it. What do you use?
domande.spiegazione: The change is permanent and the most similar page is the new product.

blocchi.testo: The same content can have several URLs: for example a category sorted by price (/te-verdi/?ordina=prezzo). For Google they're copies, and it has to guess which one to show. The canonical is a hint in the code saying which version is the main one. That way filters stay available for shoppers and Google shows the right page.
blocchi.esempio: /te-verdi/?ordina=prezzo points its canonical to /te-verdi/: only the category appears on Google.

opzioni.t: The main version of a page that has copies
That the page must not appear on Google
Where to redirect people opening the page

domande.spiegazione: The canonical doesn't hide or move anything: it says which version to treat as the real one.

blog.titolo: Noindex, robots.txt and canonical: the differences

blocchi.testo: Google measures the experience of real visits with Core Web Vitals. LCP: how long the largest element takes to appear (good under 2.5 seconds). INP: how quickly the page responds to a click (good under 200 milliseconds). CLS: how much the page shifts while loading (good under 0.1). Phones and computers are looked at separately.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie's product pages have an LCP of 4.1 seconds on phones because of a photo that's too heavy: lots of people leave before seeing the product.

domande.testo: Match each metric to what it checks.
coppie: How quickly the page responds to a click
How much the page shifts while loading
domande.spiegazione: LCP = loading, INP = responsiveness, CLS = stability.

domande.testo: If a page is fast on a computer, it's fast on a phone too.
domande.spiegazione: Phones and computers are measured separately: on phones the connection and processor are often slower.

blocchi.testo: Google Search Console (free) shows how the site performs on Google: clicks, impressions, indexed pages, errors. Google Analytics (free) shows what people do after the click. A crawler, such as Screaming Frog (free up to 500 URLs), reads the whole site and finds errors, duplicate titles, redirects. Keyword tools tell you how much and when a word is searched.
blocchi.esempio: A typical Monday: Search Console to see if anything dropped, the crawler to find out why, Analytics to understand what it costs.

domande.testo: Which tool do you use to…
coppie: Find out how many pages are on Google
Find all duplicate titles on the site
Find out how many orders come from Google
domande.spiegazione: Search Console looks at Google, the crawler looks at the site, Analytics looks at people after the click.

riepilogo: Noindex removes a page from the results; robots.txt blocks crawling.
A 301 moves a page for good; the canonical indicates the main version among copies.
Speed is measured with LCP, INP and CLS; the basic tools are Search Console, Analytics and a crawler.

finali.testo: A category disappeared from Google after a site update. What do you check first?
finali.spiegazione: If a page disappears completely, the first suspect is something excluding it from the index.

finali.testo: An LCP of 4 seconds on phones is good.
finali.spiegazione: It's over 2.5 seconds: it needs improvement, in fact it's on the edge of «poor».

finali.testo: The filtered versions of a category appear as copies. What do you use?

opzioni.t: A canonical pointing to the category

finali.spiegazione: The canonical keeps filters for shoppers and tells Google which page to show.

parole: An instruction asking Google not to show a page.
A permanent move of a page to another URL.
Indicates the main version among several copies of a page.
Google's measures of page speed and stability.
